page: Microsoft Azure ND40rs_v2 is an NDSv2-family virtual machine designed for high-performance computing and accelerated workloads. Powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this server features 40 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 Intel processor architecture. The system provides a high-density resource profile with 672.0 GB of system memory, translating to 16.8 GB of RAM per core.

The primary hardware accelerator configuration consists of eight NVIDIA V100 GPUs, delivering a combined 238 GB of video RAM. For local storage, the instance is equipped with a 2970 GB SSD. Additionally, the server supports Premium Storage and is RDMA (Remote Direct Memory Access) capable, which facilitates low-latency, high-throughput networking across multi-node clusters.

Given the inclusion of eight dedicated GPUs, massive memory capacity, and RDMA networking, this server represents a high-density hardware class. It is qualitatively structured for resource-intensive workloads where multi-GPU parallelization is required. The instance is suited for deep learning training, large-scale AI inference, high-performance computing simulations, and complex data science jobs that leverage clustered GPU resources.
